stem: A 6-year-old boy has chronic sinusitis and recurrent bronchiectasis. Examination and chest radiograph show the cardiac apex pointing to the right side of the chest. A defect in which process best explains the abnormal cardiac position?
option_A: Failed migration of neural crest cells into the outflow tract
option_B: Defective left-right dynein function during cardiac looping
option_C: Failure of septum primum and septum secundum to fuse
option_D: Failure of the aorticopulmonary septum to spiral
correct_explanation: Cardiac looping in week 4 establishes left-right polarity. Defective left-right dynein causes dextrocardia, as in Kartagener syndrome. The same ciliary defect explains the sinusitis and bronchiectasis.

A.reason: Neural crest failure causes conotruncal defects (TGA, tetralogy of Fallot, truncus), not dextrocardia.

B.reason: Correct answer

C.reason: This produces a patent foramen ovale, not abnormal cardiac position.

D.reason: Failure of the septum to spiral causes D-transposition of the great arteries.

high_yield_pearl: Dextrocardia plus sinusitis and bronchiectasis means Kartagener syndrome, a dynein defect.

stem: A newborn with cleft palate and hypocalcemic seizures is found to have a 22q11 deletion. Echocardiography shows a single arterial trunk overriding both ventricles with a VSD. Which embryologic failure best explains this cardiac lesion?
option_A: Failed migration of neural crest cells forming the truncal and bulbar ridges
option_B: Nonfusion of septum primum and septum secundum
option_C: Incomplete fusion of the endocardial cushions of the AV canal
option_D: Persistently high pulmonary vascular resistance after birth
correct_explanation: Neural crest migration forms the truncal and bulbar ridges, which spiral and fuse into the aorticopulmonary septum. Failure causes truncus arteriosus, TGA and tetralogy of Fallot. 22q11 syndromes are associated with truncus arteriosus and tetralogy.

B.reason: This causes a patent foramen ovale, not a single outflow trunk.

C.reason: This causes AV septal defect, which is associated with Down syndrome.

D.reason: This describes persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn, not a structural outflow defect.

high_yield_pearl: Neural crest failure gives the conotruncal trio: TGA, tetralogy of Fallot and truncus arteriosus.

concept_name: Patent foramen ovale and paradoxical embolism
stem: A 34-year-old woman develops a sudden left MCA stroke 5 days after a long-haul flight. Duplex ultrasound shows a femoral vein thrombus, and bubble-contrast echocardiography shows microbubbles crossing from right to left atrium when she strains. Which developmental failure explains the shunt?
option_A: Failure of septum primum and septum secundum to fuse after birth
option_B: Normal cell death creating the ostium secundum
option_C: Incomplete fusion of the endocardial cushions
option_D: Failure of the aorticopulmonary septum to fuse with the muscular septum
correct_explanation: After birth, higher LA pressure presses septum primum against septum secundum, and they normally fuse in infancy. Persistent nonfusion leaves a patent foramen ovale, present in about 25% of people. Venous emboli can cross it when right-sided pressure transiently rises.

B.reason: Cell death forming the ostium secundum is a normal step.

C.reason: This causes AV septal defect with primum ASD and cleft mitral valve.

D.reason: This causes a membranous VSD, not an atrial shunt.

high_yield_pearl: PFO is failed fusion; ASD is a true defect. Both permit paradoxical emboli.

stem: During cardiac surgery on a child, the surgeon finds a markedly dilated coronary sinus caused by a persistent left-sided venous channel. The coronary sinus is derived from which embryonic structure?
option_A: Left horn of the sinus venosus
option_B: Right horn of the sinus venosus
correct_explanation: The left horn of the sinus venosus becomes the coronary sinus.

B.reason: The right horn forms the smooth part of the right atrium (sinus venarum).

C.reason: The primitive pulmonary vein forms the smooth part of the left atrium.

D.reason: The right common cardinal vein forms the SVC.

high_yield_pearl: Left sinus horn gives coronary sinus; right sinus horn gives the smooth right atrium.

stem: A pathologist examines the outflow regions of both ventricles from a fetal specimen. She notes that the smooth-walled outflow portions of the LV and RV have a different origin from the trabeculated muscular portions. Which structure gives rise to the smooth outflow tracts?
correct_explanation: The bulbus cordis forms the smooth outflow parts of both ventricles. The primitive ventricle forms the trabeculated parts.

A.reason: The primitive ventricle forms the trabeculated parts of the LV and RV.

B.reason: The truncus arteriosus forms the ascending aorta and pulmonary trunk.

C.reason: Correct answer

D.reason: Endocardial cushions form the atrial septum, membranous IV septum and AV and semilunar valves.

high_yield_pearl: Bulbus cordis forms the smooth outflow tracts; the primitive ventricle forms the trabeculated walls.

stem: A fetal echocardiographer traces oxygenated blood returning from the placenta. Much of this blood bypasses the hepatic sinusoids and enters the inferior vena cava directly. Which structure provides this bypass?
correct_explanation: The umbilical vein drains through the ductus venosus into the IVC, bypassing the liver. It becomes the ligamentum venosum after birth.

A.reason: The foramen ovale shunts IVC blood from right atrium to left atrium.

B.reason: The ductus arteriosus shunts pulmonary artery blood to the descending aorta.

C.reason: Correct answer

D.reason: The umbilical arteries carry deoxygenated blood from the fetus to the placenta.

high_yield_pearl: Three fetal shunts: ductus venosus, foramen ovale and ductus arteriosus.

stem: A 3-day-old premature infant has bounding pulses and a continuous machinelike murmur at the left infraclavicular area. Echocardiography confirms a hemodynamically significant PDA. Which drug is most appropriate to close the duct?
correct_explanation: Prostaglandins keep the ductus open. NSAIDs such as indomethacin or ibuprofen, or acetaminophen, close it, leaving the ligamentum arteriosum.

B.reason: PGE1 and PGE2 keep the PDA open.

C.reason: Hydralazine is an arteriolar vasodilator and does not close the duct.

D.reason: Digoxin is a positive inotrope and does not close the duct.

high_yield_pearl: Indomethacin ends the PDA; PGE keeps it open.

concept_name: Left atrial enlargement and Ortner syndrome
stem: A 48-year-old woman with long-standing rheumatic mitral stenosis develops progressive dysphagia to solids and new hoarseness. Barium swallow shows extrinsic compression of the esophagus by an enlarged left atrium. Compression of which structure explains her hoarseness?
correct_explanation: The LA is the most posterior cardiac chamber. Marked enlargement can compress the esophagus (dysphagia) and the left recurrent laryngeal nerve (hoarseness, Ortner syndrome).

B.reason: The phrenic nerve innervates the pericardium, not the vocal cords.

C.reason: Esophageal compression causes dysphagia, not hoarseness.

D.reason: SVC compression would cause venous congestion, not hoarseness.

high_yield_pearl: Big left atrium: dysphagia plus hoarseness (Ortner syndrome).

stem: A 62-year-old man has chest pain with ST elevation in leads II, III and aVF. His heart rate is 38/min with complete AV dissociation. Coronary angiography shows a right-dominant circulation. Which vessel is most likely occluded?
correct_explanation: In right-dominant circulation the PDA arises from the RCA. The PDA supplies the AV node, so RCA occlusion causes an inferior STEMI with AV block.

B.reason: LAD occlusion causes anterior and septal infarction with V1-V4 changes.

C.reason: LCX gives the PDA only in left-dominant circulation, which this patient lacks.

D.reason: Left main occlusion would cause extensive anterolateral infarction.

high_yield_pearl: Inferior MI plus heart block points to RCA, which gives the PDA and AV node supply in right-dominant hearts.

stem: A patient in cardiogenic shock receives a dobutamine infusion, and stroke volume rises. Which intracellular mechanism best explains the increased contractility?
option_A: PKA phosphorylation of Ca2+ channels and phospholamban
option_B: Direct inhibition of the Na+/K+ ATPase
correct_explanation: β1 stimulation raises cAMP and activates PKA. PKA phosphorylates Ca2+ channels, increasing Ca2+ entry and Ca2+-induced Ca2+ release. It also phosphorylates phospholamban, raising SR Ca2+ storage.

B.reason: This is the mechanism of digoxin, not catecholamines.

C.reason: Ca2+ channel blockade lowers contractility.

D.reason: Reduced cAMP follows β1-blockade and lowers contractility.

high_yield_pearl: β1 leads to cAMP, then PKA, then more Ca2+ entry and SR Ca2+ storage, so contractility rises.

stem: A 55-year-old man with untreated hypertension for 15 years has concentric LV wall thickening on echocardiography. The hypertrophy is a compensatory response to chronically increased afterload. Per the Laplace law, thickening of the wall primarily reduces which variable?
correct_explanation: Wall stress equals pressure times radius divided by twice wall thickness. Increasing thickness lowers wall stress despite elevated pressure.

B.reason: Hypertrophy is a consequence of high pressure; it does not lower arterial pressure.

C.reason: Venous return is determined by volume and venous tone, not wall thickness.

D.reason: Heart rate is set by SA node automaticity.

high_yield_pearl: Wall stress = Pr / 2h, so the heart thickens to offset high pressure.

concept_name: Ejection fraction and Fick cardiac output
stem: A 60-year-old man has an LV end-diastolic volume of 140 mL and an end-systolic volume of 60 mL on echocardiography. What is his ejection fraction?
correct_explanation: SV = EDV - ESV = 80 mL. EF = SV/EDV = 80/140, about 57%, which is within the normal 50-70% range.

A.reason: 43% is ESV/EDV, which is the wrong ratio.

B.reason: Correct answer

C.reason: 70% does not match 80/140.

D.reason: 80 is the stroke volume in mL, not a percentage.

high_yield_pearl: EF = (EDV - ESV)/EDV, and normal is 50-70%.

concept_name: Ejection fraction and Fick cardiac output
stem: A catheterization lab measures oxygen consumption of 250 mL/min, arterial O2 content of 20 mL/dL and mixed venous O2 content of 15 mL/dL. What is the cardiac output by the Fick principle?
correct_explanation: CO = VO2/(CaO2 - CvO2) = 250 mL/min divided by 5 mL/dL (50 mL/L) = 5 L/min.

A.reason: This results from a unit error (dividing by 10 mL/dL).

B.reason: Correct answer

C.reason: This would need an A-V difference of 2.5 mL/dL.

D.reason: This would need an A-V difference of 2 mL/dL.

high_yield_pearl: Fick CO = O2 consumption divided by the arteriovenous O2 content difference.

stem: A 76-year-old woman has BP 168/68 mm Hg with no valvular murmur. Her SV and heart rate are normal. Which change best explains her wide pulse pressure?
correct_explanation: Pulse pressure is directly proportional to stroke volume and inversely proportional to arterial compliance. Aortic stiffening in older adults causes isolated systolic hypertension.

B.reason: Lower SV would narrow pulse pressure.

C.reason: Higher compliance would narrow pulse pressure.

D.reason: Viscosity affects resistance, not pulse pressure in this way.

high_yield_pearl: PP is proportional to SV and inversely proportional to compliance.

stem: A patient has atherosclerotic narrowing that reduces a femoral artery's radius to one-half of normal. Blood viscosity and vessel length are unchanged. By what factor does resistance to flow change?
correct_explanation: Resistance is proportional to 1/r^4. Halving the radius gives 2^4 = 16 times the resistance.

A.reason: A 2-fold change would imply r to the first power.

B.reason: A 4-fold change would imply r squared.

C.reason: An 8-fold change would imply r cubed.

D.reason: Correct answer

high_yield_pearl: R is proportional to 1/r^4, which is why arterioles control TPR.

stem: A 40-year-old man undergoes spinal anesthesia for knee surgery. Sympathetic blockade causes marked venodilation, and his blood pressure falls. Which hemodynamic change best explains the drop in cardiac output?
option_A: Decreased venous tone lowers mean systemic filling pressure and venous return
option_B: Increased inotropy raises the cardiac function curve
option_C: Increased circulating volume raises venous return
option_D: Increased total peripheral resistance reduces cardiac output
correct_explanation: Spinal anesthesia reduces venous tone, which shifts the vascular function curve downward and lowers venous return and CO. Cardiac output equals venous return at the intersection of the two curves.

B.reason: Increased inotropy would raise CO, not lower it.

C.reason: Fluid infusion raises venous return; spinal anesthesia does not.

D.reason: Sympathetic blockade lowers, not raises, vascular tone.

high_yield_pearl: Spinal anesthesia and hemorrhage lower venous return; the operating point is where the curves intersect.

stem: A 58-year-old man with dilated cardiomyopathy and dyspnea has an extra low-pitched sound in early diastole at the apex in the left lateral decubitus position. He has no systolic click. Which sound is this?
correct_explanation: S3 occurs in early diastole during rapid ventricular filling. It is associated with increased filling pressures and dilated ventricles (HF, MR, AR).

B.reason: S4 is late diastolic (atrial kick) in a stiff, hypertrophied ventricle.

C.reason: The opening snap follows mitral stenosis leaflet opening and precedes a rumble.

D.reason: An ejection click is an early systolic sound in aortic stenosis.

high_yield_pearl: S3 is early diastole in a dilated heart; S4 is late diastole in a stiff heart.

stem: A 30-year-old man has a stab wound to the chest. He is hypotensive with distended neck veins and muffled heart sounds. The JVP tracing shows a preserved x descent but an absent y descent. What is the diagnosis?
correct_explanation: The y descent (RA emptying into RV) is absent in tamponade because ventricular filling is impeded by the pericardial fluid.

B.reason: Constrictive pericarditis shows a prominent y descent.

C.reason: TR shows an absent x descent.

D.reason: AF shows absent a waves.

high_yield_pearl: Absent y means tamponade; prominent y means constrictive pericarditis.

stem: An LV pressure-volume loop shows increased peak LV pressure, increased end-systolic volume, unchanged end-diastolic volume and decreased stroke volume. Which valve lesion is most likely?
correct_explanation: In aortic stenosis, LV pressure rises to overcome the gradient, ESV rises and SV falls. EDV is unchanged if mild.

B.reason: MR lowers ESV and raises EDV and SV.

C.reason: MS lowers EDV, ESV and SV.

D.reason: AR raises EDV and SV.

high_yield_pearl: AS loop: tall and narrow, with high ESV and low SV.

stem: A 28-year-old woman has a systolic ejection murmur at the left upper sternal border. S2 is widely split and the split does not change with respiration. Which diagnosis is most likely?
correct_explanation: ASD produces a left-to-right shunt that increases RV volume and delays pulmonic closure independent of respiration (fixed splitting).

B.reason: Pulmonic stenosis causes wide splitting that varies with respiration.

C.reason: LBBB causes paradoxical splitting.

D.reason: VSD gives a holosystolic murmur, not fixed splitting.

high_yield_pearl: Fixed split S2 means ASD.

stem: A 74-year-old man with exertional syncope has a harsh systolic murmur. The S2 split is audible on expiration and disappears on inspiration. What is this pattern?
correct_explanation: Delayed aortic closure (aortic stenosis, LBBB) reverses the order so P2 precedes A2. Inspiration delays P2 toward A2 and eliminates the split.

B.reason: Wide splitting is heard on inspiration.

C.reason: Fixed splitting is unaffected by respiration.

D.reason: Physiologic splitting is present on inspiration.

high_yield_pearl: Paradoxical split: heard on expiration, with AS or LBBB.

stem: A 72-year-old man has exertional syncope, angina and dyspnea. Which examination finding is expected?
option_A: Crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur radiating to the carotids with pulsus parvus et tardus
option_B: Early diastolic decrescendo murmur with pistol-shot femoral pulse
option_C: Opening snap followed by a diastolic rumble
option_D: Holosystolic murmur radiating to the axilla
correct_explanation: Syncope, angina and dyspnea (SAD) indicate aortic stenosis. Findings are a crescendo-decrescendo ejection murmur, soft S2 and weak delayed pulses.

B.reason: This describes aortic regurgitation.

C.reason: This describes mitral stenosis.

D.reason: This describes mitral regurgitation.

high_yield_pearl: SAD: syncope, angina, dyspnea on exertion mean aortic stenosis.

stem: A 35-year-old man with a bicuspid aortic valve has an early diastolic decrescendo blowing murmur at the left sternal border. Which finding is most likely?
option_B: Pistol-shot femoral pulse with wide pulse pressure
correct_explanation: AR produces wide pulse pressure, pistol-shot femoral pulse, pulsing nail beds and head bobbing. Causes include BEAR: bicuspid valve, endocarditis, aortic root dilation, rheumatic fever.

A.reason: Pulsus parvus et tardus is seen in aortic stenosis.

C.reason: Pulsus paradoxus is seen in tamponade, constrictive pericarditis and obstructive lung disease.

D.reason: An opening snap is seen in mitral stenosis.

high_yield_pearl: AR means wide pulse pressure and an early diastolic blowing murmur.

stem: A 45-year-old woman with prior rheumatic fever has a diastolic rumble after an opening snap. Her disease progresses over several years. Which finding indicates worsening stenosis?
option_A: Shortening of the S2-opening snap interval
option_B: Lengthening of the S2-opening snap interval
option_C: Appearance of a systolic midsystolic click
option_D: Loss of the opening snap with an S3
correct_explanation: As stenosis worsens, LA pressure rises, so the valve opens earlier in diastole and the S2-OS interval shortens.

C.reason: A midsystolic click suggests mitral valve prolapse.

D.reason: S3 reflects volume overload from regurgitation, not mitral stenosis.

stem: A 17-year-old athlete has syncope during exercise and a harsh systolic murmur at the left sternal border. Which maneuver intensifies the murmur?

stem: A 24-year-old woman has a midsystolic click and late systolic murmur from mitral valve prolapse. Which maneuver moves the click later in systole?
option_D: Rapid change from squatting to standing
correct_explanation: Passive leg raise increases preload and LV volume, delaying prolapse and moving the click later. Decreased preload moves it earlier.

D.reason: Standing from squatting decreases preload, so the click is earlier.

stem: A physiologist studies SA node cells and notes slow spontaneous depolarization during phase 4 before each beat. Which current accounts for this automaticity?
option_A: Mixed Na+/K+ inward current through HCN channels (If)

stem: A trauma patient with rising intracranial pressure has hypertension, bradycardia and irregular breathing. Which mechanism explains the bradycardia?
option_A: Baroreceptor-mediated reflex to the high arterial pressure
option_D: Increased sympathetic drive to the SA node
correct_explanation: Raised ICP causes cerebral ischemia and a central sympathetic response that raises BP. Increased stretch triggers peripheral baroreceptor-induced bradycardia.

C.reason: Adenosine is a drug that slows AV conduction.

D.reason: Sympathetic drive would raise heart rate.

stem: A 9-year-old boy has periorbital and leg edema with heavy proteinuria and low serum albumin. Which Starling force change is primarily responsible?

C.reason: Raised permeability occurs with burns and infections.

stem: A 2-year-old boy becomes cyanotic during crying and squats spontaneously, with relief. He has a boot-shaped heart on chest x-ray. Why does squatting improve his cyanosis?
option_A: It increases SVR and decreases the right-to-left shunt
correct_explanation: Squatting increases SVR, reducing right-to-left flow across the VSD and sending more blood to the lungs.

B.reason: Lower SVR would worsen the shunt.

C.reason: Higher pulmonary resistance would worsen the shunt.

D.reason: The VSD is structural and does not close with posture.

stem: A cyanotic newborn of a mother with poorly controlled diabetes has a chest x-ray with a narrow superior mediastinum (egg on a string). Which defect is most likely?

B.reason: Tetralogy gives a boot-shaped heart.

C.reason: Correct answer

stem: A newborn has cyanosis and a holosystolic murmur at the tricuspid area. The mother took lithium during pregnancy. Echocardiography shows downward displacement of the tricuspid valve leaflets. What is the diagnosis?

B.reason: Tetralogy is associated with 22q11 and alcohol exposure.

C.reason: ASD is associated with Down syndrome.

D.reason: Coarctation is associated with Turner syndrome.

high_yield_pearl: Lithium leads to Ebstein anomaly.

stem: A cardiac catheterization in a 25-year-old shows oxygen saturation rising first at the right atrium, then remaining high in the RV and pulmonary artery. Which defect is most likely?

stem: A 24-year-old with an unrepaired large VSD now has cyanosis, digital clubbing and polycythemia. Which hemodynamic change explains the cyanosis?
option_A: Pulmonary hypertension makes RV pressure exceed LV pressure, reversing the shunt
option_D: Increased LV pressure raising the left-to-right shunt

C.reason: Pulmonary stenosis is a tetralogy feature.

D.reason: A greater left-to-right shunt would not cause cyanosis.

stem: A 16-year-old girl with Turner syndrome has arm hypertension, weak and delayed femoral pulses and cool legs. Chest x-ray shows notching of the ribs. What causes the rib notching?

concept_name: Persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn
